title: Guide crafting help: item slot → every recipe with ingredients and named stations
player_outcome: Talking to the Guide and pressing 'Crafting' opens your inventory and a Guide slot. Put any item in it to see every recipe it is used in, each with ingredient icons and counts and 'Required objects: Iron Anvil or Lead Anvil'. Raw station ids no longer appear.
design: Verified: TownDialog.CraftHelp (TownDialog.cs:174-187) prints one text line with raw station ids, and TownCommerce.RecipesUsing linearly scans every recipe (TownCommerce.cs:191-195) even though RecipeBook has indexes (RecipeBook.cs:38-40).

Core StationNames (Content/Index/StationNames.cs): For(station) → the display names of every TileObjectDef whose Stations contains the id, joined with ' or ' (for example 'Mythril Anvil or Orichalcum Anvil'); fall back to title-cased text. Liquids come from recipe conditions.

Core ConditionDescriber (Conditions/ConditionDescriber.cs): English for every condition type ('near Water', 'at night', 'after the Eye of Cthulhu is defeated' using the flag def name, 'in Expert mode', 'during a Blood Moon', 'in the Jungle', 'carrying 50 silver', 'the Merchant lives in town', 'at least 3 residents', 'bestiary 10% complete', 'during Christmas'...). Reused by the book, the NPC tab and drop rates.

Move the RecipeBook into Core ownership: a new GameWorld.Crafting.cs partial with a lazy Recipes property, plus Craft(PlayerEntity p, CompiledRecipe r, IReadOnlySet<string> stations, ConditionContext ctx) that raises Crafted(p, ItemStack). UiContext.Recipes becomes Game.Recipes, and the CraftingPanel crafts through Game.Craft (a one-line change). Add a Core command 'craft <item> [count]' that uses CraftingEnvironment at the player's feet (smoke and achievements).

Core RecipeLookup (Gameplay/Crafting/RecipeLookup.cs): Using(ItemDef) and Making(ItemDef) → RecipeView(Output, Count, Ingredients [(label, ItemDef icon item, count, groupItems)], Stations (names), Conditions (text), CanCraftNow?). Remove TownCommerce.RecipesUsing.

Game: RecipeCard (game/UI/RecipeCard.cs) is a reusable control: output icon, name coloured by rarity, and an ingredient row of 32 px icons with counts and item tooltips (the tooltip sits on a mouse-stop Control, not a Label, see the audit), plus 'Required objects: ...'. Cards are pooled.

GuideCraftPanel (game/UI/GuideCraftPanel.cs): a PanelContainer under the chat box with an ItemSlotView bound to a 1-slot Inventory (SlotActions Left/Right click with Inventory.Cursor) and a ScrollContainer of up to 40 RecipeCards (paged). The 'craftHelp' service entry opens it and asks the inventory to open through a new UiContext.RequestInventory event wired in WorldLauncher. On close the slot item returns via SlotActions.Stow, or drops if the pack is full.
Engine command 'ui guide_craft <item>' places a stack in the Guide slot. Probe ui.guide_recipes (in GodotCommandHost).
files_modify: game/UI/CraftingPanel.cs — craft through Game.Craft (coordinate with the UI phase rewrite)
game/Bootstrap/WorldLauncher.cs — create the panel; wire RequestInventory → InventoryScreen.SetOpen(true)
tests: RecipeLookupTests: Using(wood) contains work_bench with no station; Making(iron_pickaxe) lists stations 'Iron Anvil or Lead Anvil'; group ingredients read 'Any Wood'
StationNamesTests: every station id used by a recipe has a non-empty name
ConditionDescriberTests: every registered condition type yields non-empty text (iterate ConditionCompiler.Types with sample specs)
Smoke town.cmds: 'ui talk guide' / 'ui service craftHelp' / 'ui guide_craft wood' / 'assert ui.guide_recipes > 0' / 'ui close' / 'assert inv.wood >= 20'
verification: In game: put an Iron Bar in the Guide slot → recipe cards with icons and named anvils; closing returns the bar
risks: CraftingPanel is being rewritten by the UI phase (Terraria crafting column). Only the Craft call changes here, and the UI phase should use StationNames too.
Inventory open freezes the player (audit L, UI phase); acceptable while in dialog.
